title: Sitka Spruce: Ancient Sitka Spruces You Can Visit
meta_description: The world's tallest conifer genus, mapped three times: a record giant, a beach spruce over open air, and a wind-carved octopus on the Oregon coast.
intro: Sitka spruce grows taller than almost any other conifer on Earth, and this map holds three very different arguments for why that matters. Near Lake Quinault in Olympic National Park, the Quinault Big Spruce is a world-record specimen, roughly 58 metres tall and about 18 metres round, a straightforward giant on flat ground beside a resort. A short walk away at Kalaloch, the Tree of Life keeps almost none of the usual shape: an eroding creek has undercut its roots until the trunk hangs suspended over open air, alive and, by recent reports, still losing ground. On the Oregon coast, in Tillamook, wind rather than water has done the shaping: the Octopus Tree is a Sitka spruce whose trunk splits low into several huge limbs that arc out and back down like a candelabra, a form nobody planted and nobody can fully explain.
